body: The latter warning may be suppressed with `"-Wno-sfinae-incomplete"` if the detected GCC version is 16 or higher, but I'd rather check with others first if there's a solution that doesn't require it.

I tried this but it doesn't seem to be enough, I guess it needs to enclose the actual include too where the warning is raised.
```diff
diff --git a/core/typedefs.h b/core/typedefs.h
index 0928f8aaff..6e784bb223 100644
--- a/core/typedefs.h
+++ b/core/typedefs.h
@@ -460,9 +460,17 @@ constexpr bool is_fully_defined_v = is_fully_defined<T>::value;
 /// Enforces the requirement that a class is not fully defined.
 /// This can be used to reduce include coupling and keep compile times low.
 /// The check must be made at the top of the corresponding .cpp file of a header.
+#if defined(__GNUC__) && !defined(__clang__) && __GNUC__ >= 16
+#define STATIC_ASSERT_INCOMPLETE_TYPE(m_keyword, m_type)                                                                                                                                              \
+       GODOT_GCC_WARNING_PUSH_AND_IGNORE("-Wsfinae-incomplete")                                                                                                                                          \
+       m_keyword m_type;                                                                                                                                                                                 \
+       static_assert(!is_fully_defined_v<m_type>, #m_type " was unexpectedly fully defined. Please check the include hierarchy of '" __FILE__ "' and remove includes that resolve the " #m_keyword "."); \
+       GODOT_GCC_WARNING_POP
+#else
 #define STATIC_ASSERT_INCOMPLETE_TYPE(m_keyword, m_type) \
        m_keyword m_type;                                    \
        static_assert(!is_fully_defined_v<m_type>, #m_type " was unexpectedly fully defined. Please check the include hierarchy of '" __FILE__ "' and remove includes that resolve the " #m_keyword ".");
+#endif
 #else
 #define STATIC_ASSERT_INCOMPLETE_TYPE(m_keyword, m_type)
 #endif
```

If we need to ignore it globally, this would be done here:
```diff
diff --git a/SConstruct b/SConstruct
index 52e37b9b1a..4856875828 100644
--- a/SConstruct
+++ b/SConstruct
@@ -964,6 +964,9 @@ else:  # GCC, Clang
             common_warnings += ["-Wno-return-type"]
         if cc_version_major >= 11:
             common_warnings += ["-Wenum-conversion"]
+        if cc_version_major >= 16:
+            # We rely on this for `STATIC_ASSERT_INCOMPLETE_TYPE`.
+            env.AppendUnique(CXXFLAGS=["-Wno-sfinae-incomplete"])
     elif methods.using_clang(env) or methods.using_emcc(env):
         common_warnings += ["-Wshadow-field-in-constructor", "-Wshadow-uncaptured-local"]
         # We often implement `operator<` for structs of pointers as a requirement
```

But if we can find a way to change `STATIC_ASSERT_INCOMPLETE_TYPE` so it doesn't trigger that warning, that would be great. But it sounds to me like what GCC warns about is explicitly what we want to do here.

> But if we can find a way to change `STATIC_ASSERT_INCOMPLETE_TYPE` so it doesn't trigger that warning, that would be great. But it sounds to me like what GCC warns about is explicitly what we want to do here.

Yes, I think so too.
One thought I had was to disable the warning just for the files where we use `STATIC_ASSERT_INCOMPLETE_TYPE` - but we also use the `is_fully_defined` in `RequiredParam`, because it allows us to assert type inheritance while still allowing forward declarations, so the warning would be a problem there too.

If the warning isn't triggering on anything else except `is_fully_defined`, I would vote to just disable it — it's clearly not doing much for us.
